title: Claim-bearing source evidence authenticated by identity but not semantic content
root_cause: The F055/F056 verifier authenticated exact review/comment/reply identities but did not bind the actual Codex finding body and accepted owner-reply semantics from shared SHA/run-id substring presence.
failure_mechanism: An evidence verifier can validate object identity while leaving claim-bearing free-form content mutable or semantically interchangeable, allowing unrelated, swapped, or negating commentary to satisfy the evidence check.
violated_invariant: When free-form commentary is elevated into bounded canonical evidence, the claim-bearing content must be independently bound to governed immutable/update identity or semantically validated fail-closed; IDs and incidental tokens alone are insufficient.
trigger_conditions: A verifier consumes free-form review, comment, or reply text as evidence.
Multiple semantically distinct claims can share SHAs, run IDs, thread metadata, or other incidental tokens.
The verifier authenticates comment or thread identity separately from the exact claim-bearing body.
applicable_scope: bootstrap source-commentary reconciliation verifiers
future MimiSeek evidence adapters that elevate free-form commentary into bounded canonical evidence
non_applicable_scope: structured machine records whose complete claim semantics are already schema-bound and immutable

repository_search.notes: Issue #22 repeated the generalized family search across every accepted bootstrap-commentary reconciliation surface and the separate Development Finding Authority path. PR #26 fresh review then exposed a same-class gap: a repository/PR typo could remove a required record before validation while comment-id-only completeness and zero-selection success left the claim-bearing path usable. The remediation now derives an independent exact (role, repository, pr, surface, comment_id) inventory from the accepted reconciliation documents, compares the full effective binding set against it before filtering, and rejects any accepted snapshot identity with zero required bindings. F055/F056 body/update facts are delegated to their existing canonical authority-CI owner rather than copied. Effective coverage remains all 22 claim-bearing comments; body/update/thread/original-head adversarial checks remain fail-closed. The raw GitHub collector remains non-authoritative and Development Finding Authority remains separately externally bound. The current same-class repository instance is therefore remediated on this PR; terminal acceptance still depends on exact-head hosted gates and a fresh independent semantic review.

title: Checkout filesystem existence mistaken for tracked Git authority
root_cause: The repeat-prevention validator used Path.is_file() and filesystem globbing to accept declared guard/regression/search artifacts, so checkout-local files could satisfy a repository-authority claim.
failure_mechanism: A repository validator can accidentally elevate mutable checkout state such as .git metadata, untracked files, or tracked symlink targets into durable evidence when it checks filesystem existence instead of exact tracked Git file identity.
violated_invariant: A MimiSeek record that claims a durable repository guard, regression, discovered instance, or searched file scope must resolve to a tracked regular file in the authoritative Git working tree; checkout-only state and symlinks are not repository evidence.
trigger_conditions: A validator accepts repository-relative paths as durable evidence or prevention references.
Validation runs in a checkout containing .git metadata or possible untracked files.
Filesystem existence or globbing is used as a proxy for tracked Git identity.
applicable_scope: MimiSeek self-development registries and validators that elevate repository paths into durable authority
repository-search declarations used to close confirmed development defects
non_applicable_scope: runtime temporary paths that are explicitly non-authoritative and never recorded as repository evidence

repository_search.notes: The PR #21 validator was the current instance. Remediation resolves tracked regular files through the exact HEAD Git tree and negative regressions cover .git metadata, untracked files, staged-only files, tracked symlink escape, and equivalent searched-scope cases.

title: Mutable canonical fact duplicated across multiple owners
root_cause: PR #21 placed normative Development Repeat Prevention rules in both the BASE-designated DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL owner and a new document that independently claimed to define the same cross-chat process.
failure_mechanism: Duplicating one mutable canonical fact across multiple authoritative-looking records creates ambiguous ownership, forces coordinated edits, and allows the copies to drift even when both are initially consistent.
violated_invariant: One mutable cross-chat or evidence fact has one canonical owner. Supporting documentation or registries may reference or derive from that owner but must not independently store the same mutable canonical fact.
trigger_conditions: A new document or registry stores mutable facts already owned by an accepted canonical source.
Two authority-bearing paths must be edited together to rebind the same semantic fact.
A supporting layer can reference or derive the canonical fact instead of owning a second copy.
applicable_scope: MimiSeek canonical self-development process documentation
MimiSeek authority-bearing evidence registries and semantic-binding adapters
new supporting documents or registries that overlap accepted canonical owners
non_applicable_scope: immutable evidence indexes and historical records that point to canonical authority without redefining it
derived runtime views that do not persist a second mutable canonical copy

repository_search.notes: The original overlapping process copies remain consolidated under DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL, and the pointer-only explanatory regression remains. PR #26 fresh review found a repeat of the same ownership mechanism in evidence data: F055/F056 updated_at and body-digest facts were copied into the new semantic-binding registry even though bootstrap-commentary-authority-ci-reconciliation.json already owns and verifies them. The remediation removes those mutable copies and stores only four delegation references; the semantic layer derives effective F055/F056 bindings from the canonical authority-CI owner. A regression rejects mutable binding facts in delegated records. No other current same-fact duplicate owner was found in the searched scope.

title: Unintended repository Contents write moves exact HEAD and invalidates evidence
root_cause: The development chat selected GitHub Contents write actions for operations whose intended effect was not a repository-file byte change, allowing the Contents API to move the exact review HEAD unnecessarily.
failure_mechanism: An unintended repository-content write can move an exact-review HEAD even when the intended operation is metadata, thread/ref housekeeping, or byte-identical replacement, invalidating exact-head CI/review evidence and causing unnecessary reruns.
violated_invariant: Repository content writes in the MimiSeek development workflow are consequence-bearing and may be used only when the intended operation is an actual repository-file byte change. Non-file operations use their dedicated non-content actions, and byte-identical replacement content must not be submitted through a Contents write.
trigger_conditions: The development chat is about to call a repository Contents create/update action.
The intended operation is not an actual repository-file byte change, including PR metadata/comment/thread or branch-ref movement.
The replacement bytes may be identical or the write may introduce unrelated temporary content while exact-head CI/review evidence exists or is being established.
applicable_scope: ChatGPT-driven MimiSeek repository development using GitHub connector write actions
exact-head acceptance workflows where any branch commit invalidates current evidence
non_applicable_scope: intentional repository byte changes whose resulting HEAD is expected to require fresh CI/review

repository_search.notes: This failure family originates outside repository runtime code. Earlier PR #21 occurrences included byte-identical Contents writes (`e52c4287...`, `ee58bb51...`) and a NEW_VARIANT unintended Contents write (`e9d033ad...`). During later PR #21 remediation the already-retrieved MANUAL_ONLY guard failed four more times (`88f879ad...`, `3797079c...`, `53d6eb5d...`, `104c7303...`). During PR #26 preparation the same retrieved guard failed six additional times O008-O013, and later fresh-review remediation exposed two more same-class wrong-action Contents writes O014 (`ee9c4921...`, added `NO_SUCH_FILE`) and O015 (`85ad8127...`, added `THIS_SHOULD_NOT_EXIST`). O008-O015 are all REPEAT / GUARD_TOO_NARROW and are bound to durable issue #24 comments plus external process supplements. The final PR tree omits all accidental paths; the incident commits remain historical ancestry/process evidence. Issue #24 remains the durable unresolved boundary for strengthening the external write-intent/tool-selection fence; DFP-0004 must not return to COMPLETED until prevention is demonstrably stronger.

prevention.manual_only_reason: The consequence-bearing choice between GitHub connector Contents writes and dedicated non-content GitHub actions occurs outside repository code/CI. Until the external execution substrate exposes a machine-enforceable write-intent/no-op fence, repository CI cannot prevent the chat from invoking the wrong connector action; the canonical Development Protocol therefore carries the explicit pre-write rule.

title: Bounded follow-up accepted without durable recoverable locator
root_cause: The registry validator required BOUNDED_FOLLOW_UP to contain a non-empty follow_up_refs list but treated each element as arbitrary non-empty text.
failure_mechanism: Unresolved process debt can appear durably bounded while its follow-up pointer is not independently recoverable, allowing free-form promises such as 'done later' to satisfy CI without a stable issue or repository artifact.
violated_invariant: Every bounded follow-up must identify durable recoverable work through a supported locator: an exact MimiSeek issue URL or a tracked regular file in the exact HEAD tree.
trigger_conditions: A machine record represents intentionally unresolved development work.
Closure depends on follow_up_refs surviving chat boundaries.
The validator checks only presence/non-emptiness rather than durable locator authority.
applicable_scope: MimiSeek self-development repeat-prevention follow-up references
future MimiSeek registries that represent unresolved repository-development debt
non_applicable_scope: purely explanatory prose that is not used to satisfy a machine closure state

repository_search.notes: PR #21 current-head review found the only current machine acceptance path for follow_up_refs. Remediation restricts each follow-up to a canonical MimiSeek issue URL or tracked regular exact-HEAD file and adds malformed/foreign/free-form negative regressions plus a tracked-file positive case.

title: Unknown repeat analysis can appear completed and disappear from startup view
root_cause: The initial guard constrained UNKNOWN_PENDING_ANALYSIS against repository_search status and surfaced it in active summaries, but did not constrain the independent top-level ACTIVE/RETIRED status.
failure_mechanism: Unresolved repeat analysis can disappear across chats if any independent state dimension lets the pattern leave active retrieval before its pending analysis is resolved.
violated_invariant: UNKNOWN_PENDING_ANALYSIS is temporary fail-closed debt: it must keep the pattern ACTIVE, BOUNDED_FOLLOW_UP, durably referenced, and visible in active-pattern retrieval until reclassified.
trigger_conditions: A REPEAT occurrence uses UNKNOWN_PENDING_ANALYSIS.
Repository search status or top-level pattern lifecycle can independently suppress active retrieval.
Startup retrieval filters out RETIRED patterns.
applicable_scope: DEVELOPMENT_FAILURE_PATTERN_V1 repeat occurrences
development-start active-pattern retrieval
failure-pattern retirement
non_applicable_scope: REPEAT occurrences whose prevention failure reason is already concretely classified and whose repository search is complete

repository_search.notes: The first finding added BOUNDED_FOLLOW_UP and startup-summary visibility. A later same-class review finding on HEAD 5be33a8d showed the guard was too narrow because RETIRED could still hide pending analysis; remediation now rejects retirement while any bounded follow-up or UNKNOWN_PENDING_ANALYSIS remains and adds schema/protocol/regression coverage.

title: Historical blind evaluation can leak post-target answer-key evidence
root_cause: The proposed paired-review controls hid expected finding text from the skill but did not freeze reviewer-visible evidence surface for historical targets.
failure_mechanism: A reviewer evaluating a historical PR can read public review comments, later fixes, or dispositions created after the target state and reconstruct the answer key even when the skill itself contains no leaked finding text, falsely inflating a blind A/B result.
violated_invariant: A governed blind historical reviewer comparison must bind both arms to the same pre-target evidence cutoff, exclude post-target answer-key evidence, record the allowed evidence surface and any detected leakage, and invalidate leaked cases for blind-value claims.
trigger_conditions: A reviewer experiment uses historical PRs or other targets with known later outcomes.
The reviewer can access live public evidence beyond the target cutoff.
The result is used to support a blind comparative value gate such as OK1.
applicable_scope: MimiSeek reviewer/context/strategy experiments using historical governed cases
future operating-skill paired-review evaluation protocols
non_applicable_scope: experiments explicitly designed to test answer-key exposure as the independent variable
live targets without post-target answer-key evidence at evaluation time

repository_search.notes: The accepted SEMANTIC_REVIEWER_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN already requires expected finding/fix/disposition evidence to remain hidden and explicitly treats historical public comments/fixes as leakage risk. REVIEW_JOB_COORDINATION does not define a competing historical blind-evaluation protocol. The PR #23 research document was the current deficient instance and is remediated in the same PR.

prevention.manual_only_reason: PR #23 is research-only and no accepted production evaluation schema/harness exists yet that could mechanically constrain reviewer-visible historical evidence. A keyword/doc-presence test would not prove blind isolation. Until an evaluation harness is selected, the strongest honest prevention is the explicit research invariant plus fresh semantic review; any later production evaluation implementation should make the cutoff/evidence-surface/leakage fence executable.

title: Mutable external source locator mistaken for immutable verified content identity
root_cause: The research provenance candidate treated source URLs and nominal source versions as sufficient fields for documentation, papers, service/API material that may change in place.
failure_mechanism: A retained evidence locator can continue resolving while its content changes, allowing a previously VERIFIED skill to appear CURRENT even though the exact source content used during verification is no longer the content being observed.
violated_invariant: Every retained source-evidence item that influences operating knowledge must bind the exact verified content through an immutable revision, immutable snapshot reference, or cryptographic content digest; mutable locators and nominal versions alone are insufficient.
trigger_conditions: Operating knowledge retains evidence outside an immutable repository commit/tree.
A URL, documentation page, paper landing page, service/API description, or similar source can change in place.
Refresh/currentness logic relies on locator/version identity without exact content identity.
applicable_scope: future MimiSeek operating-knowledge provenance and refresh models
research proposals that claim exact source-bound verification/currentness
non_applicable_scope: repository-backed evidence already fully bound to an immutable commit/tree and exact retained paths

repository_search.notes: No accepted production OPERATING_SKILL provenance schema exists. Repository searches for mutable source-URL provenance fields found no competing accepted schema/current instance; the deficient candidate is confined to PR #23 research and is remediated there. A future production schema/verifier should make this exact-content identity executable rather than relying on prose.

prevention.manual_only_reason: The finding concerns a research-only candidate model before any operating-knowledge schema or refresh verifier exists. A repository string test cannot establish that arbitrary future external evidence is content-bound. The research now requires immutable per-item content identity; when production schemas/verifiers are introduced, this class should be upgraded to executable schema/verification guards.

title: Accepted PR source head conflated with resulting merge commit in evidence index
root_cause: The documentation synchronization copied the resulting PR #23 merge commit into a narrative expected_head_sha assertion even though the same acceptance section already recorded the distinct accepted source HEAD correctly. No executable cross-check linked expected_head_sha prose back to the accepted exact PR HEAD field.
failure_mechanism: Canonical acceptance documentation can carry individually valid immutable identities while a narrative merge sentence swaps their roles, creating a contradictory evidence record that looks plausible because both SHAs are real and related.
violated_invariant: Any expected_head_sha claim in the canonical acceptance index must equal the accepted exact PR HEAD for that acceptance section; the resulting merge commit must remain a separate identity.
trigger_conditions: Canonical acceptance documentation records both an accepted exact PR HEAD and a resulting merge commit.
Narrative chronology restates the merge precondition or expected_head_sha.
The identities are maintained manually without an executable relation check.
applicable_scope: docs/EVIDENCE_INDEX.md accepted PR sections
future canonical acceptance-index prose that restates merge precondition identity
non_applicable_scope: Documents that do not assert exact PR merge precondition identity
GitHub merge results already represented by structured API fields without manual role reassignment

repository_search.notes: All expected_head_sha occurrences in the current EVIDENCE_INDEX were compared with the nearest accepted exact PR HEAD. The PR #23 sentence was the only current mismatch; CURRENT_STATE and ROADMAP do not carry a competing exact merge-precondition assertion. The corrected PR #23 sentence now separates expected_head_sha=90b533fd1f2de743dfe388fc1e9747658039f1e1 from resulting merge commit c673c11bd0490b3b8218a11173e30c90d5b783a0.

title: Canonical acceptance chronology not ordered by governed source heads
root_cause: The PR #26 acceptance summary manually grouped DFA-0014 with later DFA-0015/DFA-0016 without checking each adjudication's exact source HEAD against PR #26 Git ancestry.
failure_mechanism: A canonical evidence narrative can contain individually correct adjudication identities while ordering them into the wrong temporal sequence, causing future chats to reconstruct a false remediation chronology even though the underlying immutable evidence is intact.
violated_invariant: Within numbered review/remediation chronology, adjudications from the same source PR must appear in non-decreasing Git ancestry order of their exact adjudicated source HEADs; canonical narrative must not place an ancestor finding after a descendant review step.
trigger_conditions: docs/EVIDENCE_INDEX.md summarizes multiple development adjudications for one source PR.
The adjudications were produced on different exact source HEADs.
The chronology is maintained manually rather than checked against the adjudication ledger and Git ancestry.
applicable_scope: docs/EVIDENCE_INDEX.md numbered Review/remediation chronology blocks that cite DFA identities
future canonical accepted-evidence chronology summaries derived from development adjudications
non_applicable_scope: Non-chronological reference lists that do not claim temporal order
Different source PRs with no shared Git-history ordering claim

repository_search.notes: The accepted-evidence index and its chronology/authority guards were searched for numbered review/remediation chronology that cites development adjudications. The PR #26 entry was the origin ordering defect: DFA-0014 source HEAD ca67eb94332106e59471b281b84c09dbbbadb11d precedes the 7058c8ed84f48ac7e3192e41af55ee9f838a665a source HEAD of DFA-0012/DFA-0013, while DFA-0015/DFA-0016 are later on 5ec83b959e7f40842b51a0aeaf92bbd81f607ce0. Because DFP-0010 prevention is still unaccepted on PR #27, DFA-0018 through DFA-0048 are pre-acceptance hardening findings rather than post-prevention repeat occurrences. Current prevention combines ledger plus immutable accepted-source Git ancestry checks with rendered inline normalization, strict non-partial DFA/range/HEAD identity matching, rendered accepted-head assertion normalization, and a fail-closed canonical authority profile: literal raw HTML and fenced blocks are forbidden on EVIDENCE_INDEX authority surface, list-relative indented code plus nested ATX headings are forbidden inside authoritative numbered chronology events, and unindented nonblank lazy paragraph continuation without an intervening blank line fails closed while ordinary indented continuation remains permitted. No additional same-class current repository instance was found in the searched bytes; terminal acceptance still depends on exact-head hosted gates and a fresh independent semantic review.
